outs: ledger gate baseline semantics: stale reporting + fail-closed baseline (AC-LGB1..AC-LGB8)
on

R2157: the round-ledger baseline is the gate's ONLY exemption channel, and only its happy path had ever been asserted - nothing pinned whether one entry could exempt more than its own gap, whether an entry whose gap was already healed stayed forever and turned the list into a junk drawer, which exit code a broken baseline produced, or whether an absent baseline path meant the same as --no-baseline. apply_baseline now reports stale_missing and stale_orphan, the baseline round numbers absent from the current gap sets: a stale entry is a maintenance signal, so it never flips the verdict, but it is never silently kept either. Each entry exempts exactly one round (a baseline naming R701 against a {R701,R702} gap leaves R702 red) and nothing ever suppresses a broken line. format_report prints exactly one stale line when any staleness exists and none when it does not, so the default face stays byte-identical to the R2152 contract, while --json always carries both keys. Two real defects were found and fixed in-window: load_baseline crashed with AttributeError on a top-level non-object baseline, and main's generic ValueError handler mislabelled a broken baseline as E_LGR_NO_STATE. A broken baseline now fails closed under its own code with exit 3, empty stdout, byte-identical file and no temp residue; an absent path equals --no-baseline and is never created. Deliverables: src/os/ledger_lines.py, src/os/test_ledger_baseline.py. Evidence: SUITE PASS 8/8 double-run with byte-identical evidence sha16 6f21c98c4a83c71f (run_identity judges bytes and conclusions identical); wired os-ledger-baseline(8); old os-ledger-lines 8/8 zero regression; live gate VERDICT CLEAN with an empty stale set. Same window closed the R2156 debt: battery RUNNER PASS 359/359 plus controls 7/7 in 776.5s and matrix 359 suites / 2994 criteria byte-identical.
adaptive multi-root inventory + evidence tree in the catalog (AC-LTI1..AC-LTI8)
on

R2156: the inventory catalog only ever read logs/, so every qa/*.log proof file was invisible while the census claimed the whole disk. The tool now scans a declared root set: the default single-root reading stays byte-identical, qa/*.log becomes qa-evidence and the rest of qa becomes evidence-other (both protected, never prunable), every file is counted once per inode so overlapping roots and hard links land in a duplicates counter instead of inflating totals, and a bad root spec or a missing root fails closed with no JSON at all. Growth between two readings is seen with no cache. One Windows defect fixed in-window: the scandir-cached stat reports st_dev/st_ino as 0, collapsing the tree into one inode, so the scan uses os.stat(path). Deliverables: src/os/logs_toolkit.py, src/os/test_logs_inventory.py. Evidence: SUITE PASS 31/31 double-run sha16 729292074a238996; legacy toolkit suite 163 checks green; wired os-logs-inventory(8). Honest gap: the full battery and the matrix regeneration were not run this window (the launch was cancelled by the shell pipe with no evidence file and no orphan) and are the next round first item.
double-run identity dialect helper + qa/ evidence audit (AC-RID1..AC-RID8)
on

R2153: two incompatible dialects for 'did run two agree with run one' collapse into one explicit, verified dialect - bytes or conclusions, never silently upgraded; claims are read from the body only so a product assertion is not mistaken for an evidence claim; a byte claim that does not hold is E_FALSE_BYTE_CLAIM and a declared digest is accepted against either disclosed form (whole file or payload view without the driver RUN line); a read-only audit of qa/ finds 63 pairs with zero conclusion drift and one historical artifact baselined class-wise. Deliverable: src/os/run_identity.py, state/run_identity_baseline.json, src/os/test_run_identity.py.
writer-census negative family + per-file disposition face (AC-CDN1..AC-CDN8)
on

R2151: the R1841 drift detector could name the three shell-capture dialects but had no way back - a file rebuilt in the healthy tee dialect kept flagging class-migrated forever, and the only exit was a whole-baseline re-freeze that would also mask unrelated drift. qa_writer_census.py now grows accept_reconciled plus a repeatable --accept NAME: one baselined, still-present, now-tee file is dropped from its class list (tee files are never baselined), while four refusal forms (not baselined and still bad, baselined but not rebuilt, disappeared, baseline missing) leave the baseline byte-identical and a second accept reports already-reconciled without a write. The atomic writer is one shared helper behind both the freeze and the accept face. New suite test_census_negative.py pins 12 criteria: the three negative dialects named with exit 2, the rebuilt path back to DRIFT-CLEAN, the refusal family, idempotency and determinism, no silent auto-heal, atomic-write hygiene, the audit lines and the R1841 selftest staying green. Evidence: SUITE PASS 12/12 double-run byte-identical sha16 3e67b1858537e8ed (qa/census-negative-R2151-a.log and -b.log); wired ledger-census-negative(12); the R2150 leftover tmp-sweep expected count corrected 8 to 18. Honest notes: the first negative fixture used a pure-ASCII payload whose gbk and utf-8 bytes coincide, so it classified as pwsh-capture and reddened AC-CDN1 until a Chinese sentinel was written with escapes; the first battery attempt died to a buffering pipe and was re-run through the streaming writer, where 352/353 suites were green and the single red is reconcile-daily-census cd8 shipped-clean=False - a self-reference that cannot pass before the commit which carries the changed file.
tmp sweep ownership anchors: negative-example window (AC-TSN1..AC-TSN8)
on

R2150: the birth-site sweep (R2127) deletes temp worlds behind three anchors - a name-family regex, a world signature file and an age/window gate - and none of those anchors had ever been tested against the shapes they are meant to reject, so a false match would delete another window's live world. This window closed that: has_signature now counts a signature only as a regular file that is not a link, because a bare name match let a directory merely called apimarket.db (or a junction) qualify a foreign or half-built tree. The suite grew from 10 to 18 criteria: four same-prefix foreign name shapes (apimarket with no separator, amzzz-x, APIMARKET-x, apimarketx-x) stay non-candidates on both the age leg and the battery-window leg even when they carry a real signature; a nested same-name world is invisible because the scan is root-level; all seven signature names occupied by directories leave every world non-candidate; the seven-family positive control proves the tightening kills nothing; a recording proxy over sweep() proves the delete domain equals the candidate set exactly and every negative tree is byte-identical afterwards (relative path + per-file sha256 snapshot); both legs agree; a missing root and a plain file return empty without raising; sources stay ASCII with zero network imports and the ledger-tmp-sweep label is untouched. Verification: SUITE PASS 18/18 on the first run, double run byte-identical sha16 9a362acc85d50a2c (qa/tmp-sweep-neg-R2150-a.log and -b.log, single-writer UTF-8 LF after CRLF normalisation). Same window: the daily quality crawl fetched four official pages and kept one A-graded source (the mini-program virtual payment doc for enterprises and sole traders) with three honest negatives, the benchmark sections 1/3/4 and signal W34 were refreshed, and the heartbeat rows were backfilled.
apimarket buyer-side category spend (api_buyer_category_spend)
on

R2149: the buyer side had a time axis (api_buyer_months), a lifetime aggregate (api_buyer_profile), a row face (api_library) and two statements, and the market had a per-category demand face - but nothing answered the resident's own question 'where did my money go', so a budget review or a category cap meant pulling the library, resolving each listing's category and rebucketing by hand. api_buyer_category_spend(buyer_id, include_uncategorized=True) is that mirror: a fourteen-key envelope with fourteen-key category-ordered rows and the honest uncategorized bucket last. Row authority is the PURCHASE side, which is the deliberate difference from api_category_demand: a category this buyer never bought in stays absent even when the market holds listings there, because the face answers a spending question rather than a supply question. Buckets come from the one effective-category seam, so a revise_category moves the buyer's spend in the same step it moves the catalog and demand faces, and summing every buyer's rows reproduces api_category_demand exactly.
